diagnostic_interpretation: The preimplementation PagingAliasesRetainOperandsAndCode failure proves lost operand progress on both SDKs. The accompanying FullMode test had malformed JSON and was not a semantic counterexample.

An early build exposed dependent include reordering; a comment-separated fixture include preserves declaration order. Copying staged sources with preserved old modification times then caused an incremental linker failure; all changed runtime sources were recompiled before the first implementation execution.

The first implementation run used an incorrect six-byte far-pointer fixture: selector 0x10 was placed after eight bytes instead of four. The corrected 32-bit pointer is 0x001012345678. No production change was made in response to that fixture failure.

Cold native KVM execution on the E core observed modified aliased operands. Pre-faulting only KVM stage-2 mappings made both core classes agree on the unchanged cases 0 through 4; guest page tables and original instruction bytes remain untouched. This is consistent with cold stage-2 instruction retry, not proof of a particular VM-exit sequence or an ISA core difference.
The focused green suites each pass 17 tests, including the existing seven return tests. Their counts are separate from final clean-source qualification.

native_oracle.method: A fresh VM/vCPU per original stream; two initial SREGS writes in the existing helper, no intermediate host state rewrites. KVM_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY populates only stage-2 backing. Original CPU sees the descriptor page from entry; software omits that page, retains progress and adds only missing backing on resume. Compare complete represented CPU state and all 0x40000 physical RAM bytes, including page-table A/D effects.
native_oracle.limitation: These compare an uninterrupted original instruction against software host suspension. They do not claim direct observation of an intra-instruction hardware pause.

coverage: Accepted selector/pointer values and original code survive page-table aliases, repeated pauses, zero-budget pending calls and new execution-context construction.
An empty access journal remains pending and unpaid, blocks producer polling/acceptance and consumes the instruction budget only on completion or architectural effects/fault.
Resume refuses altered full CPU state, controls, features, debug bank, access order, alignment, source body, validator and scheduler bindings before further RAM effects.
TF/RF, data watchpoints, incoming SS/STI state and newly started MOV-SS inhibition survive descriptor and event backing stops; LSS does not start a new MOV-SS shadow.
Guest descriptor faults retire the instruction before event suspension without publishing coupled offset/cache changes. Unbound null-base refusal does not consume an instruction boundary.
Descriptor accessed-write backing recovery preserves operands and code; the unchanged descriptor in this fixture does not independently prove that its earlier descriptor read was replayed.
The full-mode owner retains the same unpaid code64 instruction record; direct segment-owner validation rejects changed CPU/paging features without RAM access.
boundaries: NeverC remains a host-x64 compiler. Guest instruction operand widths and NeverD guest modes do not add a NeverC i386 source target.

The shared code64 return/event path, complete paged-source and legacy-source, instruction-boundary and SDK integration suites were rebuilt and replayed. The earlier full lower-paging qualification remains independent; untouched lower legacy owners are not recounted here.
Code64 descriptor-tail canonicality, remaining mode-aware owners, real/unreal/VM86 composition, software SMM/SGX, unbound asynchronous producers and physical SGX qualification remain open.
Production LLVM remains neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6. This work does not publish a new LLVM release or change source gitlinks.
